decision: Citations are written as inline code `source_id#anchor`, `; `-separated in one parenthetical.
reason: Anchors contain parentheses, commas and brackets; backticks delimit them exactly.

decision: Esquema rows of a sources.yaml course must resolve, not also appear in the prose.
reason: The prose-coupling rule belongs to the norm grammar; amendment 3 only asks rows to cite an anchor.

decision: Bullet ids per section as an HTML comment `<!-- bullets: … -->` under each `##` heading.
reason: Requirements 5 asks for metadata per section and fixes no syntax; a comment stays out of the rendered page.

decision: A bullet declared by a lesson must belong to that lesson's subsection.
reason: Section 5: one lesson per subsection; a stray bullet is a scope error.

decision: Stub lessons ("Lesson not written yet.") are pending: skipped by scope, counted by coverage.
reason: Coverage cannot pass before S2 writes the modules.

decision: J callout is a `:::judgement{source= ref=}` block.
reason: Requirements 4 and N2 ask for a visibly different rendering with attribution; the platform already parses `:::` directives.

decision: Snippets live as files under content/backend-in-depth/snippets/<lesson>/ with a `.run.json` record beside each; lesson blocks reference them with `snippet=` in the info string.
reason: Requirements 8.2 step 1 writes snippets as files; the record is the X evidence of section 4.

decision: Basiri et al. 2016 accepted as Tier A from the arXiv preprint the authors posted.
reason: Requirements 3.1 admits original papers the authors make freely available.

decision: Course flag `practice_scheduler: spaced` (course.yaml) opts a course in; absent keeps practice_order unchanged.
reason: Requirements 6.5/N4; other courses and the Android bundle must not change.

decision: No new table or migration: the order is derived from answered practice attempts (exam_session_id NULL, answered_at, is_correct, variant_id).
reason: The existing Attempt rows already hold everything the rule needs.

decision: Rule: unseen questions (random order), then failed questions due by now (most overdue first), then every other seen question (longest unanswered first).
reason: Unseen first; a failed question outranks settled ones only when its day has come.

decision: A failed question is due latest-answer + RETURN_AFTER_DAYS[run] days (1,3,7,15,30; last repeats), run = correct answers in a row since the last failure; a new failure resets run to 0.
reason: Simple growing interval measured from the last answer, as asked.

decision: Option order is not reimplemented: quiz options are already shuffled deterministically from each attempt seed and stored in the snapshot, so a reload shows the same order.
reason: Checked exercises/quiz.py _shuffled and the review endpoint.

decision: Mixed review = `POST /practice/review {count}` (default 20, course-wide, same scheduler); 409 PRACTICE_NOT_AVAILABLE on a course without the flag. No due counts, badges or reminders are exposed.
reason: Requirements 6.6 and rule 10 (no engagement mechanics).

decision: Frontend preset UI (by module, mixed review button, code-reading-only, generators-only filters) is left to S3; only the backend scheduler and review endpoint are wired.
reason: Presets need content kinds that do not exist yet.

decision: Subagent cap raised from 4 to 8 (4 writers, 4 verifiers) in CLAUDE.md and requirements 8.4 and 10.
reason: User instruction, 2026-11-13.

decision: Course-tier source `course-requirements` (tier `course`, product curset, version 1.2, url = repo-relative path, path ../../docs/backend-in-depth-course-requirements.md, AGPL-3.0-only, extract_allowed true, storage repo) is registered by `tech_sources.py register-file`; Markdown anchors are slugs of `#` headings; apply-licences leaves tier `course` entries alone.
reason: m00-l01's table describes requirements section 4, so it cites the course's own document; a repo file has no URL for a licence rule to match.

decision: In a course with sources.yaml the loader parses esquemas only and checks each row's `source_id#anchor` against TechSourceIndex; it builds no norm-citation scan or links for such a course.
reason: Amendment 3; norm-and-article stays mandatory for every course without sources.yaml.

decision: Question quota per lesson = max(10, min(30, F + X)); F = prose parentheticals holding only citations (outside Key points and Sources) + esquema rows, X = distinct `snippet=` blocks.
reason: Requirements 6.1: roughly 15 to 30, minimum 10, from the count of F and X facts.

decision: Java is matched against the longest Java version in versions.yaml (25.0.5) on whole dotted components: `java -version` must equal it or start with `25.0.5.`.
reason: The system JDK reports 25.0.5.0.3 (the GA tag build suffix); prefix on components accepts it and refuses 25.0.50 or 25.0.4.

decision: Kotlin 2.4.21 is provisioned from the official JetBrains GitHub release into ~/.cache/curset/toolchains/ after its published `.sha256` matches; a snippet run checks `kotlinc -version` and any other version is refused.
reason: Requirements 4: snippets run on the pinned compiler only.

decision: Every snippet command runs under `unshare -rn --`; if that probe fails nothing is executed (exit 2). Default timeout 30 s per step, configurable with --timeout.
reason: No network for snippets; Kotlin compilation needs more than 20 s of headroom.

decision: A snippet's record is `<File>.run.json` beside it (stem, not `<File>.java.run.json`); it holds commands, exit code, timed_out, stdout, stderr, stdout sha256, snippet sha256, JDK and Kotlin versions, isolation, and no timestamp.
reason: Re-running an unchanged snippet leaves the record byte-identical.

decision: A variant family is `variants/<family>.yaml` with `@@name@@` placeholders; each distractor is the stdout of the same program with one named mistake applied (`replace: [from, to]`); a grid point with fewer than three distinct distractors is skipped and reported; evidence goes to `variants/<family>.runs.json`.
reason: Distractors computed by script from typical mistakes (requirements 6.2); the quiz schema forbids extra fields, so the evidence sits beside it.

decision: check_citations resolves lesson citations only from parentheticals holding nothing but inline-code citations, esquema rows and `:::judgement ref=`; a stored anchor whose recomputed sha256 differs from anchors/<id>.json fails (version audit).
reason: Contracts 1: a citation is always inline code in a parenthetical; plain code like `Map#get` must not count.

decision: Code blocks use highlight.js core with only java, kotlin, sql, yaml, json, http, bash, plaintext registered; token colours are CSS custom properties (light, dark) in index.css; the block is a focusable region that scrolls sideways inside its own box.
reason: One library for the job; react-markdown already hands the fence's first word as the language and keeps the meta out of the DOM, so snippet= never shows.

decision: HTML comments are dropped by a remark plugin (lib/comments.ts) on lessons and Prose; other raw HTML keeps rendering as text.
reason: react-markdown showed <!-- bullets: … --> as text; skipHtml would also have swallowed literal tags such as <Enter> that other courses print.

decision: Code blocks use highlight.js core with only java, kotlin, sql, yaml, json, http, bash, plaintext registered; token colours are CSS custom properties (light, dark) in index.css; the block is a focusable region that scrolls sideways inside its own box.
reason: One library for the job; react-markdown already passes the fence's first word as the language and keeps the meta out of the DOM, so snippet= never shows.

decision: HTML comments are dropped by a remark plugin (lib/comments.ts) on lessons and Prose; other raw HTML keeps rendering as text.
reason: react-markdown showed <!-- bullets: ... --> as text; skipHtml would also swallow literal tags such as <Enter> that other courses print.

decision: The PDF prints a judgement as a violet callout opened by a bold 'Judgement from <source>' line; code blocks keep the existing sans codeBlock style (no embedded monospace face).
reason: A directive with no print rule printed nothing, so the judgement text would have vanished from the book; no mono font is embedded and adding one is out of scope.

decision: `:::judgement` attributes are validated at load, for every course, by content/judgement.py: source required and non-empty, only source and ref allowed, ref must be source_id#anchor and resolve when the course has sources.yaml; fenced code is skipped.
reason: Contracts: source required, ref an optional citation.

decision: The callout shows ref as plain text, not a link.
reason: The platform links citations only for courses with sources/normativa.yaml; a sources.yaml course serves no source page. The source URL is one tap away in the solution panel.

decision: Question `extract` (LocalizedText) and `snippet` (<lesson>/<File>.java|.kt) are QuizVariant fields with exclude=True, so no course's served or exported payload changes.
reason: Same pattern as citation, difficulty and tags.

decision: In a course with sources.yaml the solution panel follows the first citation's source: extract_allowed true gives the extract (heading title and anchor, attribution 'Licence: X', href the source URL); false gives noExcerpt reason `licence` with the licence as `detail` and the source URL; allowed but no extract written gives reason `no-extract`.
reason: Requirements 3.2 licence rule; one panel and the existing excerpt/noExcerpt payload, plus an optional noExcerpt.detail omitted when unset.

decision: The loader rejects an extract whose first citation names no registered source or a source with extract_allowed false, and a snippet that is not a file under snippets/.
reason: Contracts and requirements 3.2. That an extract is a literal substring of its anchor is the coverage script's check, not the platform's.

decision: Quiz option text holding paired backticks is rendered as markdown (OptionText); other options stay plain text; the correct-answer line of the solution panel is still plain text.
reason: Style guide: code in options is formatted as code, without touching other courses' DOM.

decision: Platform fixture backend/tests/fixtures/content/fixture-tecnico (English, published, sources.yaml, one lesson, one quiz) is baked into the image at /app/e2e-content; e2e/technical.spec.ts covers N1 and N2 at 390 and 1280 px.
reason: backend-in-depth is a draft and S1 writes no lesson content.

decision: The 13 backend generators live in tradeschool/psicotecnico/backend/ (one module per family, catalogue.py) and join the framework through registry._all_generators(); GENERATORS (the C2 thirteen) is unchanged.
reason: C2 tests and goldens iterate GENERATORS and assert 13; a separate registry keeps them byte-identical.

decision: Each generator is a BackendGenerator[Scenario]: scenario(), stem(), correct(), mistakes(), explanation(); solve() recomputes the key from the stored scenario; the build keeps psicotecnico's deal() and generate() length-position balancing.
reason: One shape, key and distractors computed by code, same contract tests as C2.

decision: Levels are 1 and 2 for every backend generator, declared with equal weight 1 in course.yaml; the course declares exercise_types [psicotecnico].
reason: No index fixes a level mix or a type weight for this course; the framework needs the type to expose gen:<id>.

decision: Citation is a typed dataclass (lesson, suggested, confirmed=None) on each generator; scripts/export_backend_goldens.py --citations lists the unfilled; the text shown to the learner never carries it (checked per item by a test).
reason: S2 module sessions fill `confirmed`; a placeholder must not leak.

decision: Every option is wrapped in one of the generator's equivalent wordings (`forms`), drawn per option, where the options' base texts differ in length by structure (capacity, retry, circuit breaker, isolation, heap).
reason: Distractors from typical mistakes are structurally longer or shorter than the key; without iid wording the key was never the longest and failed the answer-bias guards.

decision: Circuit breaker rule from resilience4j-circuitbreaker#failure-rate-and-slow-call-rate-thresholds and #create-and-configure-a-circuitbreaker: opens when failure rate >= threshold once minimumNumberOfCalls are recorded, count-based window of the last N calls, half-open evaluates the permitted calls together with the same >= rule; calls while OPEN are rejected.
reason: Implemented as the anchors state it; strict > and ignoring the minimum are the distractors.

decision: Kafka: committed offset is the next record to read (kafka-javadoc-kafkaconsumer#offsets-and-consumer-position-heading, #commitSync(java.util.Map)); lag is defined in the stem as log-end offset minus committed offset (no stored anchor defines it).
reason: Amendment 1: the assumption is stated in the question.

decision: Isolation questions are PostgreSQL 18 (pinned 18.7): matrix of pg-transaction-iso#TRANSACTION-ISO (Read Uncommitted behaves as Read Committed, Repeatable Read prevents phantoms, only Serializable prevents the write-skew anomaly) and the serialization-failure messages of #XACT-REPEATABLE-READ and #XACT-SERIALIZABLE.
reason: Version named in the stem; the matrix is stated by the anchor.

decision: Composite index question asks which columns' conditions are guaranteed to bound the scanned range (equalities on leading columns plus one inequality), ignoring skip scan, per pg-indexes-multicolumn#INDEXES-MULTICOLUMN (18.7).
reason: The anchor makes skip scan an optimisation the planner may apply, so only the guaranteed rule has one answer.

decision: Rate limiter, retry backoff with full jitter, quorum arithmetic, consistent hashing direction, Lamport/vector clocks, LRU, heap and loop complexity use the textbook rule with the model stated in the stem; suggested anchors name the topic (redis-rate-limiter, resilience4j-retry, paper-dynamo p5/p7, paper-lamport-time-clocks p4, javadoc-linkedhashmap, javadoc-priorityqueue) but none states the full formula.
reason: No stored anchor states these rules (the full-jitter formula is the AWS blog, Tier C, not stored); amendment 1.

decision: Capacity estimation is script arithmetic from assumptions in the stem (86,400 s/day, 365 days/year, decimal units); distractors are the missing factor (peak, replicas, years, bits) and unit slips.
reason: Amendment 1.

decision: Backend goldens: 50 per generator in docs/backend-verification/s1/generator-goldens/<id>.md with fingerprints in backend/tests/goldens/backend-generators-fingerprints.json (script export_backend_goldens.py), separate from the C2 files.
reason: C2 goldens must not move.

decision: Generator stems carry the full scenario and run longer than the 15 to 40 words of the style guide's form rule (an interleaving, a ring or a call sequence cannot be said in 40 words).
reason: The word range targets static prose questions; every condition the answer depends on must be in the stem.

decision: Capacity and retry-backoff options carry hedged wordings ("about", "approximately"), so every distractor keeps a relative gap of at least 20% from the key and from the other distractors (min_separation; a distractor inside the margin is dropped before the deal and the scenario is redrawn if fewer than three remain); the test scans seeds 0 to 2999 at both levels. The other families (circuit breaker, quorum, clocks, hashing, LRU, heap, loop, isolation, Kafka, composite index, rate limiter) have no hedged wording and exact discrete answers, so adjacent values are distinct answers and no margin applies.
reason: Two options within 5% of the key were both defensible under "about" (925 of 6000 capacity items, 173 of 6000 retry items); review finding 1.
